problems: Caption says 'I sprinkled iron sand': no sprinkling is shown. Frame 1 already has a full sheet of grains lying on the grass, and nothing pours them or drops them.

Caption says 'tapped it. Tap by tap': no tap is visible. No hand, tool or body touches the ground, and the grass and grains never jolt. The grains turn all at once from random to combed between storyboard frames 3 and 4 (about 1.2–1.8 s), with nothing causing it.

'Tap by tap the grains fan out' claims a gradual build-up, but after frame 4 the picture is frozen. Frames 4–16 and the 25/50/75% stills look the same, so about 8 of the 10 seconds show nothing happening.
The 'buried magnet stone' is never shown or hinted at. The viewer only sees a vague swirl left of centre, so nothing explains why the grains point the way they do.
The sand covers a sharp-edged rectangle with straight sides and square corners (every frame). That reads as a placed mat or texture, not sand sprinkled by hand.

Each grain is a big black block, like bristles or fur rather than fine sand. Many stand up on end or seem to float above their shadows (the front edge and the right corner clump in the 25/50/75% stills), so they don't look like they lie on the grass.
The 'lines' do not read as field lines. In the full-size stills they look like a combed hairy rug, and the pattern is hard to make out under the dense, dark blocks.
posts.critique: The caption describes sprinkling, tapping and a step-by-step fan-out over a magnet stone, but the film shows a ready-made rectangle of floating black blocks. It snaps into a fur-like pattern once with no visible cause and then holds still for eight seconds. Someone scrolling past would not see sand, taps or a magnet.
